history.dynasty: None (sant/sampradaya tradition; royal patronage recorded from the Maharana of Udaipur and the Maharaja of Jodhpur)
history.period: Founded 500+ years ago (early 16th century) by Shri Boyat Ji Maharaj, direct disciple of Shridev Jasnath Ji
history.summary: CSV town corrected: Shri Jasnath Asan is not in Nagaur town - it stands at Panchla Siddha ('place of deep meditation') village near Khimsar, ~60 km from Nagaur in Nagaur district. Per the ashram's own history, it was founded 500+ years ago by the great saint Shri Boyat Ji Maharaj, a direct disciple of Shridev Jasnath Ji (born 1482 at Katriyasar, lived 1539-1563 per Rajasthan-GK sources). It is regarded as a Siddh Peeth where many siddhas performed sadhana, and is one of the oldest asans of the Marwar region. The garh (fort-like ashram structure) was sponsored by the Maharana of Udaipur, Shri Jagat Singh, while the Maharaja of Jodhpur donated cultivation and grazing land; the present Adhisthata Yogi Surajnath Siddh restored and refurnished the complex. The ashram follows the Jasnathi sampradaya - a Jat-caste sect of ~700,000 followers spread over Bikaner, Nagaur, Hanumangarh and Churu districts, observing 36 rules, preaching self-control, truth, de-addiction, environmental conservation and social reform, and famous for the fire-dance (Agni Nritya) tradition. Note: the MAIN/pradhan peeth of the Jasnathi sect is at Katriyasar (Qatariyasar) in BIKANER district - this ashram is a major historic asan of the same sect, not the main peeth. The site is also known today for yoga retreats hosting Western visitors.

name: Shri Jasnath Asan
town_description: Panchla Siddha is a small village near Khimsar in Nagaur district, Marwar region - the 'place of deep meditation' where this centuries-old Jasnath ashram has stood for over 500 years, in the arid Thar-edge countryside ~100 km from Jodhpur and ~60 km from Nagaur.
